dishes.ran-sajji: A whole leg, rubbed and slow-roasted until the crust cracks and the meat gives way. Sold by the kilo, served over rice.
dishes.chicken-sulemani-karahi-1kg: Tomato, salt, green chilli and ginger. Nothing else goes in, and the karahi never leaves the flame.
dishes.beef-chapli-1kg: Pressed flat by hand, studded with tomato and egg, and shallow-fried until the edges catch. The Peshawar original.
dishes.kabli-beef-pullao: Rice steamed in the meat's own stock, sweetened with carrot and raisin. The plate a Pakhtun table is built around.
dishes.full-platter: Pulao, kababs, boti, fish and naan on one tray — the order for a table that cannot agree on anything.

story.title: Cooked slow, the Pakhtun way
story.body: At Pak Khyber Shinwari we cook the way it has always been done in the Khyber — meat, salt, tomato and fire, and nothing that gets in their way. Our dum pukht sits sealed over low coals for hours. Our karahi never leaves the flame. Our naan comes straight off the tandoor wall.
story.body2: Come sit on a charpai in the open majlis, or take a family cabin inside. Either way, the qahwa keeps coming.

about.title: The Khyber, cooked on the Grand Trunk Road
about.lede: Shinwari cooking comes from the Khyber Pass — from Landi Kotal, where the food is judged by what the cook leaves out. Meat, tomato, salt, green chilli, fire. No thickeners, no heavy masala, nothing to hide behind. Pak Khyber Shinwari cooks that way on the GT Road at Sangjani.
about.dumPukhtBody: The pot is sealed and left over low coals for hours. Nothing escapes, so the meat cooks in its own steam and falls off the bone. It cannot be hurried, which is why a whole lamb is ordered ahead.
about.karahiBody: Cooked over a roaring flame in a heavy iron karahi that never leaves the fire. Tomato, salt, green chilli and ginger — that is the whole recipe. Everything depends on the heat and the timing.
about.tandoorBody: Afghani naan pressed onto the clay wall and pulled off blistered. Bread here is not a side order; it is the plate, the spoon and half the meal.
about.tableBody: Sit outside in the majlis on a charpai the way it is done back home, or take a family cabin inside. Either way the qahwa keeps coming and nobody moves you along.
about.peoplePending: We are still gathering the details of the family behind Pak Khyber Shinwari. This section will carry their story shortly.
about.visitBody: We are on the Grand Trunk Road at Sangjani, near Multi Gardens B-17. Parcel and takeaway are available for everything on the menu.
about.pullQuote: Nothing is added that the meat does not need. That is the whole of Shinwari cooking, and the hardest part of it.
about.promiseTitle: Four things we do not compromise
about.promise1Body: Karahi and BBQ go on the fire when you order them. Nothing sits in a warmer waiting for a customer.
about.promise2Body: Ran sajji, dumba karahi and the full dum pukht lamb are sold by the kilo because we break down whole animals, not trimmings.
about.promise3Body: Afghani naan and double patiri roti come off the tandoor as they are ordered. They reach the table still too hot to hold.
about.promise4Body: Every dish on the card travels. Disposable boxes are charged at cost — Rs 50, 80 or 100 by size.
about.galleryTitle: Fire, bread and a full table
about.faq1Q: Do you do parcel and takeaway?
about.faq1A: Yes — everything on the menu can be parcelled. Disposable boxes are Rs 50 small, Rs 80 medium and Rs 100 large.
about.faq2Q: What tax is added to the bill?
about.faq2A: Government tax as printed on our menu: 5% when you pay by card, 16% when you pay cash. The website shows the exact figure before you confirm an order.
about.faq3Q: Can you feed a large family or a function?
about.faq3A: Yes. The Full Dum Pukht is a whole 10kg lamb at Rs 42,500, and the Full Platter at Rs 8,000 covers a large table with pulao, kababs, fish and naan.
about.faq4A: On the Grand Trunk Road at Sangjani, Islamabad — near Multi Gardens B-17. Call us on the number below if you are close and cannot spot the gate.
about.peopleBody: Shinwari kitchens are family businesses. The cooking is learned at home long before it is done for money, and the recipes are not written down anywhere — they are held by the people standing over the fire.
about.peopleAsk: The details below come from the restaurant itself. We do not publish a name, a date or a face we have not been given.

seating.whenTitle: The same kitchen, three different evenings
seating.when1Body: Halwa puri, paye and tandoori paratha with a thermos of qahwa. Quietest part of the day, and the naan is at its best straight off the wall.
seating.when2Body: Winter afternoons in the open majlis are the reason people drive out here. Order a karahi, let it sit on the fire, and take your time.
seating.when3Body: The busiest hours. Take a cabin or a family table, and if there are more than a dozen of you, order the dum pukht ahead so it is sealed and waiting.
seating.know1Body: The hall and the cabins are family seating. The open majlis takes everyone.
seating.know2Body: There is parking at the gate, so nobody has to stop on the Grand Trunk Road.
seating.know3Body: A whole dum pukht lamb is sealed and cooked from the morning. Call the day before.
seating.know4Body: Anything on the menu can be parcelled if you would rather eat at home.
